| Section 11.3 | `a_derived_guid_is_stable_and_well_formed` | Derived fixture identifiers are stable, input-sensitive, and carry the expected UUID version and variant bits |
| Section 11.3 | `a_manifest_round_trips` | A generated fixture manifest round-trips without losing entries, lengths, digests, or its build-derived token |
| Section 11.3 | `crates/fixtures/src/layout.rs`, `crates/fixtures/src/catalogue.rs`, `cargo xtask fixtures` | Fixture bytes and identifiers are generated deterministically from source, and the repository task writes them beneath the generated-output boundary. |
| Section 11.3 | `every_writer_is_deterministic` | Signature writers produce byte-identical images for identical inputs. |
| Section 11.3 | `generation_is_deterministic` | Rebuilding one GPT fixture from the same inputs produces byte-identical output that can be generated and cached instead of committed |
| Section 11.3 | `generation_writes_every_fixture_and_a_manifest` | Generation writes every catalogue image plus a reloadable manifest whose lengths and token match the emitted bytes |
| Section 11.3 | `hex_is_lowercase_and_padded` | Binary digests render as fixed-width lowercase hexadecimal for deterministic manifests |
| Section 11.3 | `regenerating_reproduces_identical_bytes` | Two independent generation directories receive identical tokens and byte-identical copies of every catalogue fixture |
| Section 11.3 | `regeneration_removes_a_withdrawn_fixture` | Regeneration removes withdrawn images and leaves exactly the current catalogue plus its manifest |
| Section 11.3 | `request_is_exactly_read_only_autoclear_partscan_at_512_bytes` | The request is read-only and fixes every loop configuration field used by Tier 2. |
| Section 11.3 | `the_fixture_generator_is_a_documented_task` | The fixture generator is reachable through the xtask command parser. |
| Section 11.3 | `the_linux_loop_acceptance_has_one_exact_closed_selector` | Exactly one ordered Tier-2 acceptance selector maps to the closed acceptance enum |
| Section 11.3 | `the_lvm2_checksum_is_not_an_ordinary_crc32` | The LVM2 checksum implementation is deterministic and distinct from ordinary CRC32. |
